provenance.relationship: full rewrite; no upstream file is carried over

owns: the redaction pipeline: detect, reserve, resolve, assign, rewrite
the curated structural pattern library and its validators
the Vault and its secrecy contract
optional tier gating and capability truth for ner, web and crypto
the command-line interface and the local web interface
the neutral command IR and both CLI frontends (argparse and click)
the diagnosis surface: what is detected, what is blind, what to do
the interactive terminal session and the web launcher
does_not_own: spaCy model quality or entity recognition accuracy
what a caller does with a vault after export()

crypto.note: the Fernet cipher only; vault encryption itself is base tier since CP-040

nltk.note: plus four data packages; English only; the lighter alternative to spacy

release_requirements: focused tests collect and pass without harness edits
import isolation proven under an __import__ blocker
one negative probe green per CP finding
invariants hold over a randomized scale probe
entity engine live evidence (spacy and nltk)
offset alignment proven for every engine over fuzzed text
engine interchangeability: a vault written under one engine restores under the other
every pattern's examples found, and not over-captured, in ordinary sentence positions

cli.capability_gate: none - the base tier is stdlib-only, unlike mcp

text_input.conflict: text given both positionally and with --in is an error, never a silent choice
text_input.interactive: falling through to a terminal prints a hint naming every other way in
text_input.prose: a heredoc with a quoted delimiter is the documented way to paste text containing shell metacharacters

option_grammar.long_options: full spelling only; abbreviation is refused by both frontends (CP-032)
option_grammar.end_of_options: a standalone '--' ends the options; everything after it is text, including tokens beginning with a dash
option_grammar.dash_leading_values: attach with '=' (--hide=-value); the separated form is accepted by click and refused by argparse, so '=' is the portable spelling
option_grammar.stray_options: a dash-leading positional with no '--' before it is refused, never treated as text (CP-033)
option_grammar.rule: every one of these is asserted through BOTH frontends; a difference between them is a defect, not a preference

pair.encode: text in, a pasteable prompt out; default vault, append mode
pair.decode: the model's answer in, the values put back
pair.forget: delete the vault when the conversation is over
pair.why: the two names read as one operation and must behave like it (CP-037)

engines.vocabulary: one canonical entity label set; every engine maps onto it
engines.why: spaCy says ORG where NLTK says ORGANIZATION. Passing those through raw would make the placeholder depend on which engine happened to be installed, and a vault written under one engine would not restore under the other.
engines.explicit_request: --ner is a request, not a default: an engine mode that resolves to nothing raises rather than scanning for nothing and reporting success (CP-024).

api.purpose: hand a safe prompt to any model - hosted or local - and put the values back in the reply
api.handle: portable, JSON-serialisable, secret-free repr; carries the vault this process holds
api.context_manager: Session supports 'with', clearing the vault on exit

logging.default: NullHandler at import; nothing is emitted until configure_logging is called
logging.rule: a removed value never reaches a log record - guaranteed by construction, caught by SecretFilter

vault.not_the_working_directory: a clear-text secrets file in a checkout is one 'git add .' from a commit
vault.permissions: directory 0700, file 0600, requested at creation rather than chmod-ed afterwards

modes.overwrite: default for redact; a fresh vault each run
modes.append: default for clean; seeds from the existing vault so a value keeps its placeholder across turns

vault.index: label/kind/ordinal, carries no secrets, required by append; a format-1 vault restores but cannot be appended to
vault.lifecycle: a default path plus append mode means values accumulate, so 'forget' is part of the feature rather than an extra (CP-038): report by category, delete only with --force, and never claim more than an unlink provides

encryption.construction: scrypt or pbkdf2 KDF -> split enc/mac keys -> HMAC-SHA256 CTR keystream -> encrypt-then-MAC with the label bound into the tag
encryption.fernet: --cipher fernet, needs the crypto tier; a vault written with it needs that tier to read
encryption.recorded: cipher name and every KDF parameter live in the document, so decryption dispatches and old vaults stay readable
encryption.key: CLEANPROMPT_VAULT_KEY, else a getpass prompt at a terminal; 'doctor --new-key' generates one with no dependency
encryption.limit: a standard composition, not a reviewed AES implementation; stated in the module rather than glossed

styles.placeholder: [PERSON-1]; the default, because it cannot be mistaken for a real value
styles.surrogate: an invented but ordinary-looking value for linguistic kinds; credentials keep placeholders
styles.grammar: the style is part of TagStyle and so of the grammar fingerprint, with a default-style digest deliberately unchanged so vaults written before the field remain readable

restoration.lenient: on by default; recognises the bounded set of rewrites a model applies and acts only on ones that resolve to a held label
restoration.reported: every repair is listed in RestorationResult.repaired and named in the note
restoration.why: the channel between redaction and restoration is a language model, not a pipe (CP-042)
